amendments.rule: Rule 55's correlative clause is not peculiar to a crasis. Where a **separate** `καί` answers a preceding comparative `καθώς`, `καθάπερ` or `ὡς`, that `καί` takes the whole English correlative — *so* or *even so* — and the comparative adverb keeps only *as* or *even as*. `καθὼς … καὶ ὑμεῖς` → *as … so ye* gives *so* to the conjunction at JHN.6.57 and JHN.13.33, as `ὡς … καὶ` → *As … so* does at GAL.1.9 and 2CO.13.2, and as `καθὼς ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν` → *as he is, even so are we* does at 1JN.4.17. Rule 55 already gives the reason and it does not depend on the crasis: the comparative adverb has its own English word already, and the correlative is what the `καί` writes. The corpus confirms it from the other side, `καθώς` being rendered *even as*, *as* or *according as* in all sixty-nine of its units and never taking *so*. Rule 17 heads such a unit on ***so***, the word that realizes the correlative; a supplied *even* is an intensifying helper on it under rules 7 and 11, exactly as it is where `οὕτως` takes *even so* at JHN.3.14, JHN.5.21, JHN.5.26 and JHN.14.31 and where `ναί` does at REV.1.7. So do not head such a unit on *even* merely because *even* is the more direct gloss of `καί`: that gloss is what a bare *even* answers to where no *so* competes, as at 2CO.11.12 and EPH.2.3, and it does not carry where the ASV writes the correlative out. Where the ASV writes **no** correlative and renders the comparative together with its answering `καί` by a bare *even as*, that is exactly where the gloss does carry: the `καί` is `aligned` to *even* and headed on it, and the comparative keeps a bare *as* as its own unit, as `καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς` → *even as we* does at 2CO.11.12, `ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί` → *even as the rest* at EPH.2.3, and `καθὼς καὶ ἐγένετο` → *even as it came to pass* at 1TH.3.4. Do not give *even as* whole to the comparative and leave the `καί` `unrepresented`: rule 65's English-side test empties an intensifying `καί` only where the ASV writes no word for it, and a written *even* is such a word. Where the ASV writes a word of the particle's **own** — ***also*** — the bare-*even* arm does not apply. That word is the καί's under rule 65, and the comparative keeps as its own unit, headed on *as*, whatever the ASV wrote for it and no more: *even as* whole where the ASV writes the *even*, as `καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς` → *even as we also* does at 1TH.3.6 and 1TH.3.12, and a bare *as* where it writes none, as `καθὼς καὶ προείπαμεν ὑμῖν` → *as also we forewarned you* does at 1TH.4.6. A written *also* is evidence that the particle is realized, and never evidence that an *even* the ASV did not write is owed to the comparative. Rule 76's availability test is what forces this — a particle the ASV has already spent on *also* is not a word the supplied *even* can belong to — and rule 100 settles the identical division for `οὕτως … καί` → *even so … also* unanimously across thirteen units, the adverb keeping the whole correlative and the particle taking only *also*. So do not stretch the `καί` discontinuously over *even … also*, and do not read a written *also* as licence to strip *even* from the comparative. A comparative with **no** answering `καί` is the contrast and keeps *even as* whole under rules 7 and 11, no other source token standing to claim the supplied *even*, so a chapter writing both — `καθώς` alone as *even as* and `καθὼς καί` as *even* plus *as* — is following rule 24's habit and not two analyses. The test is not merely whether a `καί` stands in the construction but which English word the ASV wrote for it: a written *so* is the correlative arm and is the `καί`'s, a written *also* is the particle's and leaves the comparative whatever the ASV wrote beside it, *even as* or a bare *as*, a bare *even as* with no other word for the particle splits into the `καί`'s *even* and the comparative's *as*, and no answering `καί` at all leaves *even as* whole on the comparative. Never decide it from how the same comparative was rendered where a different word, or none, stood.
amendments.why: 1TH.4.6 `καθὼς καὶ προείπαμεν ὑμῖν` → *as also we forewarned you* is a shape rule 82's *also* arm had not considered: the ASV writes *also* for the particle and no *even* at all. The arm as it stood prescribed in terms that "the comparative keeps *even as* whole", which is a factual claim about the English and is false here, and the closing summary repeated it. The amendment leaves the placement principle untouched — a written *also* is still the particle's, and the comparative is still headed on *as* — and only makes the arm say what rule 82's own English-side test already requires, that the comparative takes the words the ASV actually wrote. It contradicts no corpus unit: 1TH.3.6 and 1TH.3.12, the arm's own precedents, wrote the *even* and keep *even as* whole under the amended wording exactly as before. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule so the over-broad sentence is corrected where a verse pass will read it.

conventions: Stacked articles before participles divide by the count of English relativizers the ASV wrote. Where two articles stand before two participles and the ASV writes a relativizer for each — ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι → *we that are alive that are left* at 4:15 and 4:17 — each article takes its own *that* under rules 32 and 90, the pronoun slot being already filled by the expressed ἡμεῖς, and each participle keeps its supplied copula and lexical word. Where the article instead follows an expressed nominal head that already carries its own determiner — τὰ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ εἰδότα at 4:5, τὸν θεὸν τὸν … διδόντα at 4:8, οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες at 4:13 — the article is unrepresented under rule 31 and the single relativizer is the participle's helper.

A supplied English subject for an infinitive the ASV expands into a finite clause rides with the infinitive under rule 74: *man* at 4:6, *one* at 4:9, *ye* at 4:10 and 4:11. An expressed accusative subject instead takes the English subject word as its own unit, ὑμᾶς at 4:1, 4:3 and 4:13. The consequence at 4:6 is that *no man* splits — μή keeps the bare *no*, as οὐ keeps the *no* of *no need* at 4:9 and μή the *no* of *no hope* at 4:13, and *man* belongs to ὑπερβαίνειν. Keeping *no man* whole on the negator remains defensible.

The chapter's five supplied *even*s divide by the class of the token that carries what the *even* introduces, not by the ASV's italics. The correlative ones are aligned — to καί at 4:1, 4:5 and 4:13 under rule 82's bare-*even* arm, and inside οὕτως' *even so* at 4:14 under rule 100 — while the appositional *even* at 4:3 is `added` under rule 105's article-carrier arm, the appositive being carried by an article rule 20 has already emptied and by no expressed preposition.

report: Checked all 30 candidate lemma groups. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one word differently, licensed by the source or by the English the ASV wrote: kai takes *and*/*also*/*even*/*indeed* or nothing by rules 65, 82 and 100; en, eis, peri and dia follow the ASV's own preposition words; anistemi takes *again* only where the ASV writes it (rule 106); kyrios and theos differ only in whether an article stood to take the determiner (rules 21, 23, 51).

The two configurations worth reading closely both hold. (a) Articles before participles: an article standing after an expressed nominal head that already carries its own determiner is unrepresented and the single relativizer is the participle's helper (4:5 τὰ … εἰδότα, 4:8 τὸν … διδόντα, 4:13 οἱ … ἔχοντες, rule 31); an article whose pronoun slot is filled by an expressed ἡμεῖς keeps the relativizer the ASV wrote for it (4:15, 4:17, rules 32, 90). Two articles, two written *that*s; one article-and-participle pair, one written *who*. The count of English relativizers divides them, and both readings are inside rules 31 and 90.

(b) Supplied infinitive subjects. 4:6 *no man*, 4:9 *one*, 4:10 and 4:11 *ye* all ride with the infinitive under rule 74, and an expressed accusative subject takes its own English word at 4:1, 4:3 and 4:13. That is what makes μή keep a bare *no* at 4:6, matching οὐ → *no* at 4:9 and μή → *no* at 4:13. Consistent, and the 4:6 note already concedes the whole-*no man* reading.

The `added` blind spot the briefing warns about: the chapter has one `added` unit, the appositional *even* at 4:3, and four aligned *even*s (4:1, 4:5, 4:13 on καί; 4:14 inside οὕτως' *even so*). The division is by carrier — rule 105's article arm against rules 82 and 100's correlatives — not an inconsistency. No supplied word is folded in one verse and added in another.

BSB disagreements: none is an error. 1TH.4.5 τά, 1TH.4.8 τόν and 1TH.4.13 οἱ are the documented rule 31 convention, where we give the relativizer to the participle and BSB marks the article represented. 1TH.4.4 τό is emptied by the possessive ἑαυτοῦ under rule 20 and BSB renders the phrase otherwise. 1TH.4.8 καί is unrepresented because the ASV writes no word for it (rule 65), while BSB writes *also*. Nothing here should move to raise the rate.

Textual units: 8, six selected and two underdetermined (4:6 s014 κύριος, 4:8 s011 καί), both carrying readings the ASV translates or leaves unwritten on ordinary grounds, so rule 97 is not in play anywhere in the chapter.
